Changelog

fcutils 0.1.2

Results are unchanged.

  • multi_chain(verbose = FALSE) does not print the series it extends.
  • Faster growth rates and aggregation, with identical results. For monthly, quarterly and annual data with no missing dates, pcmp(), the to-date growth functions and ptd_gr() take a lag by position within each series instead of through tsbox::ts_lag(), and aggr() and faggr() take grouped means or sums instead of tsbox::ts_frequency() (when missing values sit only at the start or end of each series). Anything else goes through tsbox as before. On 200 quarterly series over a century: aggr() 0.4 s (4.5 s in 0.1.0), pcmp() 0.14 s (3.4 s), ytd_gr() 0.3 s (3.3 s), ptd_gr() 0.4 s (3.6 s). A test compares each fast path with tsbox on random series.
  • Faster on large banks, with identical results: conv_long(), which most functions call first, skips tsbox::ts_regular()’s checks when no date is missing (0.9 s to 0.07 s on 200 quarterly series over a century), and multi_chain() places each chained series back by date instead of a join per series. On that bank multi_chain() takes 0.7 s instead of 3 s, aggr() 2.7 s instead of 4.5 s and pcmp() 1.5 s instead of 3.5 s.
  • Less fixed cost per call, with identical results. conv_long() no longer asks tsbox::ts_summary() for the name of a single series that already has one, and find_start() and find_end() take the first and last date with a value directly. On one quarterly series conv_long() takes 4 ms instead of 9 ms and find_end() 5 ms instead of 13 ms; every function that starts with conv_long() gains about 4 ms.
  • get_series_exp() combines the downloaded series in one step instead of one pair at a time (200 series: 0.02 s instead of 2 s).
  • ytd_cum(), ytd_gr(), fytd_cum(), fytd_gr(), mtd_cum(), mtd_gr(), ptd_cum() and ptd_gr() share one implementation. Old and new give identical results on monthly, quarterly and daily data in every format.
  • plot_comp_2() and plot_comp_3() share one implementation; the index panel is the only difference.

fcutils 0.1.1

Results are unchanged, except where faggr() used to fail.

  • ts_rebase() is renamed rebase(), because the ts_ prefix marks tsbox functions. No other installed package exports a rebase().

  • faggr() aggregates all series at once instead of each series and year separately: 0.4 s instead of 33 s for 20 quarterly series over a century. It no longer stops on a fiscal year with no values (a series that starts or ends with missing values).

  • aggr() and pcmp() aggregate or compute all series at once, and conv_long() reads series names from the id column instead of ts_summary(). On a bank of 200 quarterly series over a century, aggr() takes 3.5 s instead of 4.5 s and pcmp() 2.0 s instead of 3.5 s; most of what remains is tsbox::ts_frequency() and tsbox::ts_regular().

  • get_series() and get_series_exp() share their request, naming and format code. An unknown rename or format now stops with a message.

  • The code is split into files by topic, and an internal helper replaces the block that returned results in the input’s class in 19 functions.

fcutils 0.1.0

Breaking changes

  • The bank is set by options, not by package data. make_xts(), addf() and the other functions that need a bank read getOption("fcutils.bnk_start") and getOption("fcutils.bnk_end"), and stop with a message if they are not set. Set them once, for example in setup.R:

    options(
  fcutils.bnk_start = as.Date("1970-01-01"),
  fcutils.bnk_end = as.Date("2070-12-31")
)

    The datasets bnk_start and bnk_end are gone.

  • to_ymd() reads a fixed set of forms and stops with an error naming any value it cannot read, where it used to return NA or guess. Accepted: years (2019), quarters (2019.4, "2019Q4", 201904), months ("2019M10", "2019-10") and days ("2019-10-15", 20191015, Dates). Months cannot be numbers, because 2019.10 equals 2019.1.

  • p() ends at the last day of the period given as its end: p(2019.4, 2026) is "2019-10-01/2026-12-31", not .../2026-01-01.

  • index() is renamed ts_rebase(), because it masked zoo::index() and xts::index(). There is no deprecated alias: it would keep masking them, and its help page would overwrite the site’s reference index. Replace index(x, ...) with ts_rebase(x, ...).

New functions

  • extend() continues a series past its last observation: through anchor values (type = "level"), through anchors on its annualized growth rate (type = "growth"), or with the growth of another series (type = "chain"). Linear or Stineman interpolation, optional loess smoothing.
  • get_series_src() downloads series from FRED, Statistics Canada, the Bank of Canada, e-Stat and EIA.
  • set_api_key() stores a key for the session or in the keyring; set_udaman_token() now calls it. Keys never appear in error messages or warnings.

New arguments

  • multi_chain(): method = "diff" adds y’s changes to x’s level; direction = "forward" or "backward" chains only one way; match = "stem" pairs UR_AT_US_A with UR_AT_US_SOLA.
  • disagg(extend_with): a series or "last_growth" extends the series before interpolating, so the result does not bend toward zero growth at the ends. The result is cut back to the series’ own periods.
  • interpol(pattern = NULL) interpolates linearly.
  • addf() takes a table of ramps (columns start, end, from, to), or points as formulas: addf(2026.3 ~ 0, 2027.4 ~ -0.3, 2030.4 ~ 0).
  • extend() takes anchors as formulas, 2026.4 ~ 4.4, so dates need no quotes.
  • plot_fc(rate = FALSE) plots changes instead of growth rates.

Fixes

  • AtoQ() and QtoA() rename only the frequency ending of a name (_SOLA to _SOLQ), not the same letters elsewhere in it.
  • multi_chain() matches the .x and .y suffixes only at the end of a name.
  • multi_chain() accepts series stored as integers.
  • save_plot_list() finds the pandoc that comes with Quarto.

Other

  • Tests (testthat 3) cover the exported functions.
